options.text: <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> is formed by heating <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> to <math><mn>170</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>

<math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> is used in the estimation of CO

<math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> combines with <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> to form <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow></msub></math> . When heated above <math><mn>75</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> , it <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> decomposes to form <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math>

solution.text:
Here statement B is incorrect as I2O5 is unstable to heat
It decomposes when heated to 300°C .
2I2O5→300°C2I2+5O2
Rest other statements are correct as follows
(i) 2HIO3→170°CI2O5+H2O
(iii) I2O5 oxidizes CO to CO2 quantitatively at room temperature, liberating I2 , which can be titrated with sodium thiosulphate.
I2O5+5CO→5CO2+I2
(iv) 2I2+3O3→I4O9
4I4O9→>75°C6I2O5+2I2+3O2
